symptom: Synthetic Node 22.16.0 reproduction showed that mutable ambient Date.parse and Date.prototype.toISOString could relabel a noncanonical generatedAt offset string and an impossible bounded scope calendar date as canonical. The validator used both ambient methods after own-data graph preflight. No private evidence or production execution was involved.
lesson: Validating a claimed UTC instant or date with ambient Date.parse and Date.prototype.toISOString permits caller-realm prototype mutation to change canonical admission without changing the evidence content digest. This is a syntactic integrity gap only; even a correct canonical date is not an independent clock or K-source attestation.
guardrail: Capture native Date constructor, parse and toISOString at module initialization and call the captured intrinsics during fixed-schema canonical checks. Regress offset-format generatedAt and impossible calendar scope dates while ambient Date methods are mutated; preserve normal valid input and digest behavior. Keep generatedAt untrusted and outside contentDigest by v0.1 contract. No K rights/finality, scoring, merge or production authority follows.
